text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- Delegates of the Jewish-American "Anti defamation League B'nai B'rith", which opposes racism and anti-semitism, met with Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti and parliamentarians in Berne on Thursday. Their speaker said it is Switzerland's moral duty to admit to its past and that a return to "business as usual" is not possible.
- Swiss Federal Railways wants to carry 105,000 trucks up to four meters high through the Alps annually starting 1999, and to extend the limit thereafter.

- The documents found by a security guard that were to be shredded at Union Bank of Switzerland were from the Eidgenossischen Bank, which UBS took over in 1945. The bank, one of the seven biggest in the country, operated as a trade bank doing business mainly with Germany.
- Basle pharmaceuticals group Roche posted an 11 percent rise in sales to 15.96 billion Swiss francs for 1996.
- In a major restructuring plan, the Toni Group will cut 250 jobs and partially or completely shut down five production plants. Its nearly 50 shops will be sold to the Usego-Hofer-Curti Group.
- Standard + Poors downgraded Union Bank of Switzerland's rating from AAA to AA+.

- The Federal Banking Commission is demanding a written report on the course of events at Union Bank of Switzerland's archives. The head of the archives who ordered the shredding of documents was apparently in bad health and his competence is in question.
- Switzerland's Manor Group posted a sales decline of 2.8 percent to 2.64 billion Swiss francs for 1996.
